components.note: 日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.
日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'

example.hanzi: 明早八点我们要出发去机场。
example.pinyin: Míngzǎo bā diǎn wǒmen yào chūfā qù jīchǎng.
example.english: Tomorrow morning at eight o'clock we need to leave for the airport.
example.fact: The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to three scientists who identified the genes controlling the body's circadian clock, the internal timer that makes many people feel groggy at dawn and alert by mid-morning. Their research traced the rhythm to a feedback loop of proteins that rise and fall roughly every 24 hours, even in constant darkness. This same clock is why jet lag disrupts sleep after crossing time zones.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ancient texts were written on bound bamboo strips, and 第 originally referred to the sequential order of such strips, giving rise to its meaning 'ordinal number' (as in 第一, first).

The oracle-bone form of 六 pictured a simple hut or shelter with a peaked roof; that picture was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the number six, and the original 'shelter' meaning was dropped entirely.

example.hanzi: 他在班里排名第六。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bān lǐ páimíng dì liù.
example.english: He ranks sixth in his class.
example.fact: Many biologists argue Earth is now in the midst of a sixth mass extinction, following five prehistoric die-offs including the one that ended the dinosaurs 66 million years ago. Unlike those earlier events, which were driven by asteroid impacts or volcanic activity, the current wave of species loss is linked mainly to habitat destruction, climate change, and overexploitation by humans. Some estimates suggest species are vanishing at tens to hundreds of times the natural background rate.

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 我每天骑自行车去上班。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān qí zìxíngchē qù shàngbān.
example.english: I ride my bicycle to work every day.
example.fact: Pound for pound, the bicycle is one of the most energy-efficient machines ever built: a cyclist converts roughly a quarter of their pedaling energy into forward motion, far more efficient than walking or driving. In the 1980s, China had so many bicycles on its roads that it earned the nickname 'the Kingdom of Bicycles,' with hundreds of millions of riders at the time.

components.note: 犭 (dog/animal) — historically linked to a wary, hesitant animal, extended to mean 'as if, similar to.'
尤 (yóu) is an exact match for the sound of 犹.
太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'

example.hanzi: 他的犹太祖先在二十世纪初移民到了美国。
example.pinyin: Tā de Yóutài zǔxiān zài èrshí shìjì chū yímín dàole Měiguó.
example.english: His Jewish ancestors immigrated to the United States in the early twentieth century.
example.fact: The Dead Sea Scrolls, a collection of ancient Jewish texts including the oldest known copies of the Hebrew Bible, were discovered largely by chance in 1947 when a Bedouin shepherd threw a rock into a cave near Qumran and heard it shatter pottery. The roughly 900 manuscripts, dated from the third century BC to the first century AD, were preserved for two millennia by the region's extremely dry climate.

components.note: 木 (wood/tree) — 标 originally referred to the tip of a tree, later coming to mean 'mark, sign'
票 (piào) gives a sound close to 标's reading biāo
士 (a scholar/gentleman) — represents a person of learning and ambition.
心 (heart/mind) — the mind and aspirations of a scholar gave 志 its meaning 'purpose, will, ambition.'

example.hanzi: 熊猫是中国的国家标志之一。
example.pinyin: Xióngmāo shì Zhōngguó de guójiā biāozhì zhī yī.
example.english: The panda is one of China's national symbols.
example.fact: The Nike 'swoosh' logo, now one of the most recognized brand marks in the world, was designed in 1971 by graphic design student Carolyn Davidson, who was paid just $35 for the work. Nike's founder reportedly wasn't thrilled with it at first, but the company later gave Davidson stock as thanks once the brand took off.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蜘 (as in 蜘蛛, spider) names a small crawling creature.
知 (zhī) gives the sound — an exact match with 蜘's reading.
虫 (insect) — 蛛 names a small creature, the spider.
朱 (zhū) gives the sound — an exact match with 蛛.

example.hanzi: 墙角有一只很大的蜘蛛。
example.pinyin: Qiángjiǎo yǒu yī zhī hěn dà de zhīzhū.
example.english: There is a very large spider in the corner of the wall.
example.fact: Spider silk is, by weight, stronger than steel and tougher than Kevlar, able to stretch to nearly 40% of its length before breaking without snapping. Scientists have long tried to mass-produce synthetic versions of it, since spiders themselves are too territorial and cannibalistic to farm efficiently. A single web strand thick enough to stop a passenger plane would theoretically require an enormous colony working in coordination — something researchers have only approximated with genetically engineered silkworms and bacteria.

components.note: 犭 (dog/animal) — 狗 names an animal, the dog.
句 (jù) gives a sound distantly related to gǒu, having drifted apart over time.
尸 (body) — 屁 relates to a bodily function.
比 (bǐ) gives a sound only distantly related to pì today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 别说这些狗屁话了,赶紧干活。
example.pinyin: Bié shuō zhèxiē gǒupì huà le, gǎnjǐn gànhuó.
example.english: Stop talking this nonsense and get to work.
example.fact: Dogs' noses contain up to 300 million olfactory receptors, compared to about six million in humans, letting them detect scents at concentrations of parts per trillion. This extraordinary sense of smell is why dogs are trained to sniff out everything from explosives and narcotics to early-stage cancers and diabetic blood-sugar crashes, often before any device can.

components.note: 汉 is a simplified form of 漢, pairing the water radical 氵 with a component that named the river valley tied to the Han dynasty and Han Chinese identity.
保 (to protect) — 堡 describes a structure built for defense.
土 (earth) — earthen 土 walls built for defense 保 gave 堡 its meaning 'fort, fortress.'

example.hanzi: 他午饭点了一个汉堡和薯条。
example.pinyin: Tā wǔfàn diǎnle yī ge hànbǎo hé shǔtiáo.
example.english: He ordered a hamburger and fries for lunch.
example.fact: Despite its name, the hamburger's exact origin is disputed, but its name traces back to Hamburg, Germany, where 19th-century immigrants brought a style of minced, salted beef called 'Hamburg steak' to the United States. The dish was later placed between two pieces of bread for portability, likely by German-American vendors at fairs and lunch counters around the turn of the 20th century.

meanings: to feel a sense of urgency

components.note: 着 began as a variant form of 著 (zhù), which paired 艹 (grass) with the phonetic 者; over time the top of 者 wore down into a shape resembling 羊, and this new form 着 split off to carry the everyday senses 'to wear, to touch, to arrive.'
目 (eye) sits at the base of 着, tying the character to the idea of fixing one's gaze or attention on something — a sense later extended into the aspect particle marking an action still in progress.
心 (heart/mind) — 急 relates to an anxious or urgent state of mind
刍 (chú) gives a sound distantly related to 急's reading jí, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 别着急,慢慢来。
example.pinyin: Bié zháojí, mànman lái.
example.english: Don't worry, take your time.
example.fact: When the brain perceives a threat, the amygdala triggers a rapid release of adrenaline and cortisol, redirecting blood flow toward muscles and away from digestion — the 'fight or flight' response first described by physiologist Walter Cannon in the early 20th century. Chronic anxiety keeps this system activated far longer than it evolved for, which is why prolonged stress is linked to problems like high blood pressure and weakened immunity.

components.note: 冫 (water/ice) — 冲 relates to liquid, as in pouring or rinsing with water
中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to 冲's reading chōng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.

example.hanzi: 他一时冲动买了那辆车。
example.pinyin: Tā yīshí chōngdòng mǎile nà liàng chē.
example.english: He impulsively bought that car.
example.fact: In the late 1960s, Stanford psychologist Walter Mischel ran what became known as the 'marshmallow test,' offering young children one treat now or two if they could wait 15 minutes alone in a room with it. Decades of follow-up research linked the children's ability to resist immediate impulse with later outcomes like academic performance, though more recent studies suggest family stability and household resources play a larger role than the test alone implied.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 妈妈用带子把包裹绑好了。
example.pinyin: Māma yòng dàizi bǎ bāoguǒ bǎng hǎo le.
example.english: Mom used a strap to tie up the package.
example.fact: The three-point seatbelt, now standard in cars worldwide, was invented in 1959 by Swedish engineer Nils Bohlin at Volvo. Volvo made the patent freely available to every other car manufacturer, a decision credited with saving an estimated one million lives in the decades since.

meanings: to perform on a musical instrument

components.note: 氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time
天 (sky, standing in for the ruler above) suggests something reported upward to the emperor, the root of 奏's old meaning 'to present a memorial.'

example.hanzi: 她在音乐会上演奏了一首钢琴曲。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuèhuì shàng yǎnzòule yī shǒu gāngqín qǔ.
example.english: She performed a piano piece at the concert.
example.fact: The oldest known musical instruments are flutes carved from vulture bone and mammoth ivory, found in a cave in southwestern Germany and dated to roughly 40,000 years ago. Their finger holes were spaced carefully enough that researchers have been able to reconstruct and actually play reproductions, suggesting music-making is nearly as old as modern humans themselves.

components.note: 木 (tree) — traditionally read as a tree that has borne fruit.
立 (standing) — standing close by to watch it grow, evoking closeness and nurture, extended to 亲's meaning 'close, dear; parent, relative.'
目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 我亲眼看到了那场车祸的发生。
example.pinyin: Wǒ qīnyǎn kàndàole nà chǎng chēhuò de fāshēng.
example.english: I saw that car accident happen with my own eyes.
example.fact: Psychologist Elizabeth Loftus's research beginning in the 1970s showed that eyewitness memory is far less reliable than most people assume — simply changing the wording of a question, like asking how fast a car was going when it 'smashed' versus 'hit' another car, measurably altered what witnesses later recalled. Her work has since been cited in thousands of legal cases and helped reveal that even confident, detailed eyewitness accounts can be partly or entirely false.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 富 relates to a well-stocked household, prosperous under its own roof
畐 (fú) gives a sound close to 富's reading fù, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.

example.hanzi: 他年纪很小的时候家里就很富有。
example.pinyin: Tā niánjì hěn xiǎo de shíhòu jiālǐ jiù hěn fùyǒu.
example.english: His family was already wealthy when he was very young.
example.fact: Nearly all of the gold ever mined throughout human history — an estimated 190,000-plus metric tons — would fit into a cube roughly 22 meters on each side, small enough to sit within a typical soccer field. Because gold is virtually indestructible and rarely discarded, most of it mined over thousands of years, including from ancient Egyptian and Roman times, is still in circulation today, recycled into new jewelry, coins, or electronics.

components.note: 予 (to give) — 幻 is drawn as an inverted, mirror-image form of 予, picturing something turned upside down or not as it seems, giving 幻 its meaning 'illusion, fantasy.'
见 (to see, perceive) — relates to 觉's meaning 'to feel, sense, perceive.'
⺍ is a small graphic element serving as the phonetic hint, though its link to jué's modern sound has faded after centuries of change.

example.hanzi: 长期缺乏睡眠可能会导致幻觉。
example.pinyin: Chángqí quēfá shuìmián kěnéng huì dǎozhì huànjué.
example.english: Long-term lack of sleep can lead to hallucinations.
example.fact: Charles Bonnet syndrome causes people with significant vision loss — from conditions like macular degeneration — to see vivid, detailed hallucinations of people, patterns, or animals that aren't there, even though they know rationally that the images are not real. Researchers believe the visual cortex, deprived of its usual steady stream of input, essentially starts generating its own imagery, a phenomenon first described by the Swiss naturalist Charles Bonnet in 1760 after observing it in his own grandfather.

components.note: 圭, made of two 土 (earth) stacked together, depicts a handful of mortar or soil.
寸 (a hand/small measure) — sealing something shut with packed mortar gave 封 its meaning 'to seal, to close.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 这本杂志的封面是一张著名摄影师拍的照片。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn zázhì de fēngmiàn shì yī zhāng zhùmíng shèyǐngshī pāi de zhàopiàn.
example.english: This magazine's cover is a photo taken by a famous photographer.
example.fact: The very first issue of Time magazine, published in March 1923, featured retired U.S. Speaker of the House Joseph G. Cannon on its cover — chosen not for major news but simply because he was about to retire and made for a recognizable face. Time's red-bordered cover design, adopted decades later, has since become one of the most enduring visual brands in publishing history.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赚 relates to earning money.
兼 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to 赚's reading zhuàn, having drifted apart over time.
钅 (metal) — 钱 relates to money, since early Chinese coins were made of metal
戋 (jiān) gives a loose sound connection to 钱's reading qián

example.hanzi: 他靠做生意赚钱养家。
example.pinyin: Tā kào zuò shēngyì zhuànqián yǎngjiā.
example.english: He earns money running a business to support his family.
example.fact: The world's first paper currency was issued in China during the Tang and Song dynasties, around the 7th to 11th centuries, initially as promissory notes among merchants before the government took over printing it directly. Centuries later, when Marco Polo described paper money to Europeans in the 13th century, many considered the idea of trading mere paper for goods almost unbelievable.

components.note: 冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'

The oracle-bone form of 六 pictured a simple hut or shelter with a peaked roof; that picture was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the number six, and the original 'shelter' meaning was dropped entirely.

example.hanzi: 我们周六去公园野餐吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōuliù qù gōngyuán yěcān ba.
example.english: Let's go have a picnic in the park on Saturday.
example.fact: Saturday is the only day of the week in English whose name comes directly from a Roman god — Saturn — rather than from a Germanic or Norse deity, unlike Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. The seven-day week itself likely originated with the ancient Babylonians, who associated each day with one of the seven visible celestial bodies known at the time, including the sun, moon, and five planets.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.
俞 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tōu, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.
俞 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tōu, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他偷偷把礼物放进了她的包里。
example.pinyin: Tā tōutōu bǎ lǐwù fàng jìnle tā de bāo lǐ.
example.english: He secretly put the gift into her bag.
example.fact: The mimic octopus, discovered off the coast of Indonesia in 1998, can imitate the appearance and movement of at least fifteen other sea creatures, including venomous lionfish, sea snakes, and flatfish, to sneak past predators unnoticed. It changes not just color and skin texture but also body posture and swimming style depending on which animal it is impersonating.

components.note: 又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
扌 (hand) — fighting back with bare hands
亢 — the throat, a vulnerable point defended while resisting

example.hanzi: 两支球队在决赛中激烈对抗。
example.pinyin: Liǎng zhī qiúduì zài juésài zhōng jīliè duìkàng.
example.english: The two teams fiercely competed against each other in the final.
example.fact: The human immune system wages a constant, largely invisible war against pathogens, and one of its key weapons, the antibody, can take on roughly 10 billion different molecular shapes generated by randomly shuffling a limited set of genes. This combinatorial trick lets the body recognize and resist an almost limitless variety of viruses and bacteria it has never encountered before, without needing a separate gene for each one.

components.note: 土 (earth) — relates to 城's meaning 'city, wall,' since city walls were built of earth.
成 (chéng) gives the sound — 城 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.
保 (to protect) — 堡 describes a structure built for defense.
土 (earth) — earthen 土 walls built for defense 保 gave 堡 its meaning 'fort, fortress.'

example.hanzi: 这座城堡建于中世纪,至今仍屹立不倒。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngbǎo jiànyú zhōngshìjì, zhìjīn réng yìlì bùdǎo.
example.english: This castle was built in the Middle Ages and still stands today.
example.fact: Neuschwanstein Castle in Bavaria, built in the late 19th century for King Ludwig II of Bavaria, was never intended as a serious military fortress — it was designed largely for aesthetics and privacy, complete with modern conveniences like running water and central heating unusual for its time. Its fairy-tale silhouette later directly inspired the design of Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

components.note: 阝 (hill) — 降 originally related to coming down a hill or slope
夅 (jiàng) gives the sound — an exact match with 降's reading jiàng
艹 (grass/plant) — 落 relates to leaves or plants falling
洛 (luò) gives the sound — 落 is also pronounced luò, an exact match

example.hanzi: 飞机将在十分钟后降落。
example.pinyin: Fēijī jiāng zài shí fēnzhōng hòu jiàngluò.
example.english: The plane will land in ten minutes.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted only 12 seconds and covered about 120 feet, roughly the wingspan of a modern Boeing 747, before touching back down on the sand at Kitty Hawk. Orville Wright piloted that first flight, while Wilbur ran alongside, and the brothers took turns on four short flights that day, the longest lasting less than a minute.

components.note: 乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 警方最终抓到了那名杀人犯。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zuìzhōng zhuā dàole nà míng shārénfàn.
example.english: The police finally caught the murderer.
example.fact: Fingerprint identification became a standard forensic tool after Argentine police officer Juan Vucetich used it to solve a murder case in 1892, matching a bloody thumbprint at the crime scene to the suspect, a mother who had killed her two children. It was the first criminal case in the world solved using fingerprint evidence, years before fingerprinting became routine in police departments elsewhere.

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 他平常很少喝酒。
example.pinyin: Tā píngcháng hěn shǎo hējiǔ.
example.english: He rarely drinks alcohol under normal circumstances.
example.fact: The idea of the statistical 'average person' was popularized in the 1830s by Belgian astronomer and statistician Adolphe Quetelet, who applied methods used to track measurement errors in astronomy to human traits like height and weight. His concept of l'homme moyen, or 'the average man,' laid groundwork for modern statistics but has since been criticized because no single real person is actually average across every measurement at once.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 按 relates to pressing something with the hand
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 按's reading àn, differing only in tone
手 (hand) — 摩 describes rubbing something with the hand.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 做完按摩后我感觉身体轻松了很多。
example.pinyin: Zuò wán ànmó hòu wǒ gǎnjué shēntǐ qīngsōng le hěn duō.
example.english: After the massage, I felt much more relaxed.
example.fact: Massage is described in the Huangdi Neijing, or Yellow Emperor's Inner Canon, one of China's oldest medical texts compiled around 2,000 years ago, which recommended rubbing and pressing the body to treat various ailments. Similar practices appear independently in ancient Egyptian tomb paintings and Greek medical writings, suggesting massage arose as a healing method across multiple early civilizations without shared contact.

components.note: 木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 这个问题本身就很复杂。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí běnshēn jiù hěn fùzá.
example.english: This problem itself is very complicated.
example.fact: In 1931, mathematician Kurt Gödel proved his incompleteness theorems, showing that in any sufficiently powerful mathematical system, there will always be true statements that the system itself cannot prove using its own rules. Gödel's proof cleverly works by constructing a statement that essentially refers to itself, an idea similar to a sentence that says 'this sentence cannot be proven true.'

components.note: 疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating
犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 警方正在审问一名主要疑犯。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài shěnwèn yī míng zhǔyào yífàn.
example.english: The police are interrogating a main suspect.
example.fact: The legal principle that a suspect is presumed innocent until proven guilty traces back at least to Roman law, but it was formally cemented in many modern legal systems through documents like England's Magna Carta of 1215 and later the French Declaration of the Rights of Man in 1789. Despite its long history, the presumption of innocence still varies significantly in how it is actually applied across different countries' courts today.

components.note: 女 (woman) — 奴 originally described a woman kept as a servant in a household.
又 (a hand) — standing beside the master's hand 又, the woman 女 gave 奴 its meaning 'slave, servant.'
A hand shape.
Represents grain being handled, linked to labor and servitude.

example.hanzi: 历史书详细描述了古代的奴隶制度。
example.pinyin: Lìshǐ shū xiángxì miáoshùle gǔdài de núlì zhìdù.
example.english: The history book describes ancient slavery systems in detail.
example.fact: Historians estimate that the transatlantic slave trade forcibly transported over 12 million enslaved Africans to the Americas between the 16th and 19th centuries, with roughly 1.8 million dying during the ocean crossing itself. Britain formally abolished slavery throughout most of its empire in 1833, and the payments made to former slave owners as compensation were so large that the British government only finished paying off the associated debt in 2015.

components.note: 走 (to walk, to run) — 赶 relates to pursuing or hurrying, both forms of movement.
干 (gān) gives a rhyme close to gǎn, with the tone shifted.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 他跑得很快,很快就赶上了前面的人。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài, hěn kuài jiù gǎnshàngle qiánmiàn de rén.
example.english: He ran very fast and quickly caught up with the person ahead.
example.fact: The ancient Greek philosopher Zeno of Elea devised a famous paradox around the 5th century BC arguing that the swift Achilles could never actually catch up to a slower tortoise given a head start, because by the time he reached the tortoise's starting point, it would have moved slightly further, and so on infinitely. The paradox wasn't fully resolved until the development of calculus, which showed how infinitely many shrinking time intervals can still sum to a finite amount of time.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吓 relates to a shout or cry, as when someone is frightened.
下 (xià) gives the sound — an exact match with 吓.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 那部电影的结局真的很吓人。
example.pinyin: Nà bù diànyǐng de jiéjú zhēn de hěn xiàrén.
example.english: That movie's ending was really scary.
example.fact: The human startle reflex is one of the fastest reactions the body produces, triggering a blink and muscle tensing within about 100 to 150 milliseconds of a sudden loud noise — faster than a person can consciously register what caused it. Neuroscientists trace this reflex to a simple, ancient neural circuit in the brainstem, which explains why even people who know a scare is coming, like in a haunted house, still can't help but jump.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early spears and rifle stocks were made of wood.
仓 (cāng) gives a sound close to qiāng, sharing the same rhyme.
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查昨晚的枪击事件。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zuówǎn de qiāngjī shìjiàn.
example.english: The police are investigating last night's shooting incident.
example.fact: Gunpowder was invented in China around the 9th century, originally by alchemists searching for an elixir of immortality rather than a weapon. It took several more centuries for the mixture of saltpeter, sulfur, and charcoal to evolve from fireworks and incendiary devices into the propellant used in early firearms, which then spread along trade routes to the Middle East and Europe by the 13th century.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) shows movement.
万 (ten thousand, suggesting a great distance) shows a big stride, giving 迈 its meaning 'to step, to stride.'
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

尔 is a simplified, cursive-derived form of the traditional 爾, whose ancient shape depicted an ornamental woven lattice or window pattern; that concrete image was later dropped as the character was borrowed to write the pronoun 'you, that' and, in transliterations, the syllable ěr.

example.hanzi: 我的邻居迈克尔是一名医生。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de línjū Màikè'ěr shì yī míng yīshēng.
example.english: My neighbor Michael is a doctor.
example.fact: The name Michael comes from the Hebrew Mikha'el, meaning 'who is like God,' and it has remained one of the most enduring given names in Western history, borne by archangels, kings, and popes alike. It was the most popular boy's name in the United States for most of the 1970s through the 1990s, a run of popularity unmatched by almost any other name in that period.

components.note: 力 (strength/effort) — the exertion behind the achievement.
工 (work/labor) — results produced through skillful labor, giving 功 its meaning 'achievement, merit, skill.'
大 (a grown man) — the figure being depicted.
一 (a hairpin) — worn across the top of the head to mark a coming-of-age ceremony, giving 夫 its meaning 'man, husband.'

example.hanzi: 他从小就在学习中国功夫。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù zài xuéxí Zhōngguó gōngfu.
example.english: He has been learning Chinese kung fu since childhood.
example.fact: The Shaolin Temple in Henan Province, China, founded around 495 AD, became closely associated with martial arts training partly out of necessity — monks in the remote mountain temple needed to defend themselves from bandits and, according to tradition, developed exercises to stay fit during long periods of meditation. Its style of combat training later influenced dozens of distinct martial arts across East Asia.

components.note: 乡 is a simplified form of the traditional 鄉, whose ancient shape showed two people kneeling on either side of a shared food vessel — a picture of a community eating together — which gave 鄉/乡 its meaning 'village, hometown, countryside.'
木 (tree/wood) — many early villages were built among or from trees and wood
寸 (cùn) gives a sound close to 村's reading cūn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 他退休后搬到乡村居住。
example.pinyin: Tā tuìxiū hòu bāndào xiāngcūn jūzhù.
example.english: After retiring, he moved to live in the countryside.
example.fact: In 2007, for the first time in recorded history, more than half of the world's population lived in cities rather than rural areas, a threshold the United Nations projects will rise to roughly two-thirds by 2050. The shift has been especially dramatic in China, where the urban population share roughly tripled between 1980 and 2020 as tens of millions of people moved from the countryside into rapidly growing cities.

components.note: 宀 (roof/house) — relates to 完's meaning 'complete, finish,' as in a fully built house.
元 (yuán) was the phonetic base; the pronunciation later shifted to wán, so only a partial rhyme remains today.
敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 考古学家发现了一个几乎完整的古代花瓶。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā fāxiànle yī ge jīhū wánzhěng de gǔdài huāpíng.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered an almost completely intact ancient vase.
example.fact: Sue, discovered in South Dakota in 1990, is the most complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton ever found, with about 90% of its bones recovered — an extraordinary rarity in paleontology, where most dinosaur fossils survive as only scattered fragments. The skeleton sparked a legal battle over ownership that eventually resulted in a 1997 auction where the Field Museum in Chicago won it for $8.36 million, the highest price ever paid for a fossil at the time.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 苏 relates to certain aromatic plants and to reviving, coming back to life
稣 (sū) gives the sound — 苏 is also pronounced sū, an exact match
木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
A stylized drawing of orchid blossoms and leaves growing up from the ground.

example.hanzi: 他去苏格兰旅行时参观了很多古老的城堡。
example.pinyin: Tā qù Sūgélán lǚxíng shí cānguānle hěn duō gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
example.english: When he traveled to Scotland, he visited many ancient castles.
example.fact: Scotland is home to more than 600 million liters of whisky maturing in casks at any given time — more than a hundred liters for every person living in the country — because the spirit legally must age in oak barrels for at least three years before it can be called Scotch whisky. Some of that whisky is lost each year to evaporation through the porous wood, a phenomenon distillers poetically call 'the angels' share.'

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.

example.hanzi: 别太在意别人的看法。
example.pinyin: Bié tài zàiyì biérén de kànfǎ.
example.english: Don't care too much about what other people think.
example.fact: Psychologists have documented what's called the 'spotlight effect' — the tendency for people to dramatically overestimate how much others actually notice or care about their appearance and mistakes. In one well-known 2000 study, participants asked to wear an embarrassing T-shirt in front of strangers guessed that about 50% of onlookers would remember it, when in reality fewer than 25% did.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 嘴 refers directly to the mouth, or a beak-like spout.
觜 (zī) gives a sound distantly related to zuǐ, having drifted apart over time.

巴's ancient form is usually read as a picture of a coiled snake with a raised head; that image faded as the character was borrowed for unrelated meanings and sounds, including its use in 嘴巴 where it simply marks 嘴 as a full word for 'mouth.'

example.hanzi: 他张开嘴巴打了个大大的哈欠。
example.pinyin: Tā zhāngkāi zuǐba dǎle ge dàdà de hāqian.
example.english: He opened his mouth and let out a big yawn.
example.fact: The human mouth hosts more than 700 different species of bacteria, making it one of the most microbially diverse habitats on the entire body, second only to the gut. Most of these microbes are harmless or even beneficial, helping to break down food and defend against harmful invaders, though an imbalance among them is linked to problems like cavities and gum disease.

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'

example.hanzi: 在这个团队里,他一直是老大。
example.pinyin: Zài zhège tuánduì lǐ, tā yīzhí shì lǎodà.
example.english: In this team, he has always been the boss.
example.fact: For much of European history, the legal principle of primogeniture automatically passed a family's land, titles, and wealth to the eldest son, a system designed to keep estates intact rather than splitting them among multiple heirs. The practice shaped centuries of political and economic power in places like medieval England, and echoes of it persist today in some royal succession laws, though most have since shifted toward absolute primogeniture regardless of gender.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.

example.hanzi: 这条大道两旁种满了梧桐树。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo dàdào liǎngpáng zhòngmǎnle wútóngshù.
example.english: This avenue is lined on both sides with plane trees.
example.fact: Yonge Street in Toronto was once listed in the Guinness World Records as the world's longest street, stretching about 1,896 kilometers (1,178 miles) north from Lake Ontario, though later research revealed the measurement had mistakenly combined it with a separate highway. Its origins trace back to 1793, when it was built partly as a military supply road.

components.note: 手 (hand), shown twice, side by side — two hands pressed together in a gesture of respect, giving 拜 its meaning 'to bow, to pay respects.'
讠 (speech) — 访 relates to visiting someone to speak with them or ask questions.
方 (fāng) gives a sound distantly related to fǎng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 下周我要去拜访一位老朋友。
example.pinyin: Xià zhōu wǒ yào qù bàifǎng yī wèi lǎo péngyou.
example.english: Next week I'm going to visit an old friend.
example.fact: U.S. President Richard Nixon's 1972 visit to China ended over two decades of diplomatic isolation between the two countries and was watched by an estimated one billion people worldwide through television broadcasts. Nixon later called the trip 'the week that changed the world,' and it paved the way for the two nations to establish full diplomatic relations in 1979.

components.note: 言 (speech) — an older semantic link to talking at length.
厂 (chǎng) gives a sound distantly related to zhān, having drifted apart over time.
女 (woman) — 姆 names a woman who cares for children.
母 (mǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 姆's reading mǔ.

其 (originally a winnowing basket) sits beside 斤 (an axe) — 斯 originally depicted splitting or cutting something apart with an axe, a sense now mostly lost as the character shifted to the demonstrative 'this' and to transliterating foreign names and sounds like sī.
斤 (axe) contributes the action of cutting or splitting that originally defined 斯's meaning.

example.hanzi: 詹姆斯是这支球队最重要的球员。
example.pinyin: Zhānmǔsī shì zhè zhī qiúduì zuì zhòngyào de qiúyuán.
example.english: James is the most important player on this team.
example.fact: In 2023, LeBron James became the NBA's all-time leading scorer, surpassing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's record that had stood for nearly 39 years. James reached the milestone while also holding records for career minutes played and games started, a combination that reflects both his scoring ability and his unusually long-lasting durability across two decades in the league.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
互 depicts two hooked or interlocking shapes, holding onto each other to show mutual connection.

example.hanzi: 两国同意在经济上相互合作。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó tóngyì zài jīngjì shàng xiānghù hézuò.
example.english: The two countries agreed to cooperate with each other economically.
example.fact: Clownfish and sea anemones share one of nature's clearest examples of mutualism: the fish gain protection from predators by hiding among the anemone's stinging tentacles, to which they are immune thanks to a protective mucus coating, while the anemone benefits from the fish chasing off potential predators and parasites. Neither species is thought to be able to thrive as easily without the other in the wild.

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — 样 originally referred to a kind of tree, later broadening to mean 'kind, appearance, way.'
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — 样 is pronounced yàng, matching aside from tone.
木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'

example.hanzi: 科学家从月球上带回了岩石样本。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā cóng yuèqiú shàng dài huíle yánshí yàngběn.
example.english: Scientists brought back rock samples from the moon.
example.fact: The Apollo missions brought back a total of about 382 kilograms (842 pounds) of lunar rock, soil, and dust samples between 1969 and 1972, and much of it remains sealed in original, untouched containers at NASA today. Scientists deliberately preserved a portion unopened, anticipating that future analytical techniques not yet invented would be able to extract more information than was possible at the time of collection.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 决 originally described breaching a dike or channel to let water burst through, a sense extended to 'to decide, resolve' as in cutting through hesitation.
夬 (guài) is close in sound to 决's reading jué, both descending from a shared Old Chinese root.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

example.hanzi: 他决不会向困难低头。
example.pinyin: Tā juébù huì xiàng kùnnán dītóu.
example.english: He will never bow to difficulties.
example.fact: The second law of thermodynamics states that the total entropy, or disorder, of an isolated system will never decrease over time — one of the few laws in physics considered essentially inviolable. Physicist Arthur Eddington once wrote that if a theory disagrees with this law, 'there is nothing for it but to collapse in deepest humiliation,' underscoring how central it is to modern physics.

components.note: 黑 pictures a face or window blackened by soot rising from a fire 灬 below — giving 黑 its meaning 'black, dark.'
邦 (a nation/state) — a community bound together
巾 (a flag/cloth) — a banner people rally around to support one another

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了黑帮之间的斗争。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle hēibāng zhījiān de dòuzhēng.
example.english: This movie tells the story of a struggle between criminal gangs.
example.fact: The Sicilian Mafia is believed to have emerged in the mid-19th century, partly as informal groups of armed guards hired by absentee landowners to protect citrus and wheat estates from bandits, gradually evolving into organized criminal networks with their own codes of conduct. American Prohibition in the 1920s later gave organized crime groups in the United States, like Al Capone's Chicago outfit, a massive new revenue stream from illegal alcohol.

components.note: 户 (door, household) — 肩 relates to a family member returning home.
⺼ (flesh/body) — meat carried home over one's 肩 (shoulder) gave the character its meaning.
⺼ (flesh) — 膀 names a part of the body.
旁 (beside) contributes to the character's form, describing something at the body's side, like the upper arm or a wing.

example.hanzi: 他把包扛在肩膀上。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ bāo káng zài jiānbǎng shàng.
example.english: He carried the bag on his shoulder.
example.fact: The shoulder is the most mobile joint in the human body, able to rotate through a wider range of motion than any other joint, largely because the socket is shallow compared to joints like the hip. That mobility comes at a cost, though — the shoulder is also one of the most frequently dislocated joints, precisely because its loose-fitting design trades stability for a wider range of movement.

components.note: 宣 depicts a grand hall (宀) with an open, radiating space inside, evoking a palace where proclamations were made.
亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.

example.hanzi: 政府发布了新的宣传海报。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ fābùle xīn de xuānchuán hǎibào.
example.english: The government released a new propaganda poster.
example.fact: The famous 'I Want YOU for U.S. Army' recruitment poster, depicting Uncle Sam pointing directly at the viewer, was created by illustrator James Montgomery Flagg during World War I and reused during World War II, becoming one of the most reproduced images in American history. Flagg reportedly used his own face as a model for Uncle Sam to save money on hiring someone else.

components.note: 严 is a simplified form of the traditional 嚴, whose top originally showed 吅 (two mouths, i.e. loud, repeated shouting) issuing strict orders — the source of 严's meaning 'strict, severe, rigorous.'
木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这所学校对学生的纪律要求非常严格。
example.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào duì xuésheng de jìlǜ yāoqiú fēicháng yángé.
example.english: This school has very strict discipline requirements for students.
example.fact: Ancient Sparta subjected boys as young as seven to an extraordinarily strict state-run training system called the agoge, which emphasized physical endurance, deliberate hardship like minimal food and clothing, and unquestioning obedience to prepare them for a lifetime as soldiers. The system was so demanding and singularly focused on producing warriors that Sparta, despite its military reputation, left behind comparatively little literature, art, or architecture compared to other Greek city-states.

components.note: 大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.
力 (strength) — 励 relates to exerting effort or spurring on strength in others, 'to encourage.'
厉 (lì) gives the sound — an exact match with 励.

example.hanzi: 公司给表现优秀的员工发放了奖励。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī gěi biǎoxiàn yōuxiù de yuángōng fāfàngle jiǎnglì.
example.english: The company gave rewards to employees with excellent performance.
example.fact: Psychologist B.F. Skinner's mid-20th-century experiments with pigeons and rats in 'Skinner boxes' showed that behavior reinforced by rewards, even irregular or unpredictable ones, tends to be repeated more persistently than behavior rewarded every single time. This principle, called operant conditioning, later influenced everything from classroom teaching methods to the variable reward mechanics used in modern slot machines and mobile games.
